title: AI Cash Flow Forecaster
tagline: See cash gaps before they happen.
summary: Helps small business owners forecast 30/60/90-day cash flow using sales history, invoices, payroll, fixed costs, payment schedules, and upcoming revenue.
businessProblem: Owners discover cash shortfalls when checks bounce or payroll is due — not weeks earlier when they could adjust spending, chase collections, or delay hires.
outcome: A rolling 30/60/90-day cash projection updated weekly showing expected inflows, committed outflows, projected balance, and flagged low-cash weeks with suggested actions.
whoItsFor: SMB owners managing cash manually in spreadsheets or checking accounts without a dedicated CFO — especially businesses with payroll, rent, and uneven revenue.
aiInputs: Outstanding AR with due dates and payment history
Fixed monthly costs and known large payments
Current bank balance and recent transaction patterns
aiOutputs: Narrative explanation of biggest cash drivers
Suggested actions (delay expense, accelerate collections, draw reserve)
noCodeTools: Google Sheets cash model + ChatGPT monthly refresh
Float or Pulse app with manual AI summary paste
Zapier: QuickBooks + Plaid → Sheets → GPT narrative
lowCodeTools: n8n weekly: Plaid + QBO pull → OpenAI forecast → email
Google Sheets + Apps Script + OpenAI API
Causal or Finmark export + Claude analysis
customBuildStack: Time-series forecast model + OpenAI narrative layer
Node.js cron with encrypted token storage
Dashboard in Retool or internal Next.js app
implementationSteps: Connect bank via Plaid and accounting via QuickBooks or Xero
Export 12 months sales history from POS or accounting
Document fixed costs and payroll schedule in a config sheet
Build prompt template for weekly projection with structured JSON output
Run in review mode for 4 weeks — compare projections to actuals
Set low-balance alert thresholds and delivery channel (email/Slack)
systemBehavior: Runs weekly or on-demand — not real-time intraday trading
Read-only on financial systems — never initiates payments
Uses conservative assumptions for unknown AR collection dates
Flags uncertainty ranges, not single-point false precision
Logs assumptions used each run for auditability
risks: Forecasts are only as good as input data — stale books produce wrong projections
Not a substitute for professional cash management or lending decisions
Bank feed delays can miss recent large transactions
Seasonal businesses need 12+ months history for reliable patterns
